selection_rationale: Reference studio condensers found in French studios, schools, radio, film and classical recording: the Neumann line (U 87 Ai, already in the TekPractice catalog, plus TLM 103/102/107, U 47 fet i, KM 184 and the tube M 149 and U 67), AKG C414 XLS (9-pattern workhorse), Schoeps Colette CMC 6 with MK 4 and MK 41 (references in French radio and film), Sennheiser RF condensers (MKH 8040, MKH 50) and vintage-design tube mics (Telefunken ELA M 251E and C12). Selection was limited to models whose documents could actually be read: the shared web-search budget ran out mid-task, and several manufacturer sites (AKG, Audio-Technica) returned 403 or render specs only via JavaScript (DPA, Rode, Shure KSM32C), so those candidates were swapped for fully sourced alternatives.

devices.technology: Cardioid small-diaphragm condenser with permanently fixed capsule modelled on the original CK 1, transformerless output (per AKG spec sheet).
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: AKG's spec sheet says the C 451 series dates back to 1969 and the B keeps the rising CK 1 character; a standard hi-hat, overhead and acoustic guitar mic in studios and on tour.
